newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe police teargas university students.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe police teargas university students.

text.p: Zimbabwean riot-control police threw teargas cannisters to disperse university students on Tuesday who were planning a demonstration over government delays in paying their allowances, witnesses said.

They said police had earlier sealed off the campus to stop the students from the University of Zimbabwe from marching into central Harare, but the situation later deteriorated when some of the students threw stones at them.

"We were planning a demonstration because our payout is a week late and we cannot go off for the Easter holidays without money. The police sealed off the campus in anticipation of the demonstration. Some people started throwing stones at them and they started gassing us," a student told Reuters.

"They said we should go to our halls of residence but how can we go there when they are throwing the gas in there as well," he added, turning to flee as police, wielding batons and teargas cannisters, continued to pursue the students on campus.
Scores of university staff streamed out of their offices, many of them choking on the teargas that the police had thrown into the administration buildings.
University Vice Chancellor Graham Hill, who later went into a meeting with some of the policemen, declined to comment.
